the_ownership_question.framing_offered: A = Hermes holds, engine becomes a pool supplier. B = FI-003 holds, Hermes becomes delivery only. C = combine, one owner.
the_ownership_question.auditor_view: C is correct in structure. As written it is insufficient, because the collision that caused today's damage is not ownership — it is TWO CLOCKS.
the_ownership_question.the_actual_hazard: the engine carries its own _chrono(). The canonical lane carries chron_events.json. Two independent clocks produce two different numbers for the same event, and that is how 377 and 21 can coexist in one system on one day.
the_ownership_question.non_negotiable_term: the engine's _chrono() must be DELETED, not repaired. A supplier of content does not own time. If it keeps a clock, C re-creates the defect it is meant to resolve.
the_ownership_question.second_term: the artifact path must be content-addressed (ALPHA-ZEN-MORNING-hash8.png) or the ledger must carry superseded_by, or the cycle log stays unverifiable past the next render.
the_ownership_question.self_disqualification: the auditor does not assign ownership. Per the authority envelope the executor may never issue its own envelope, and an auditor recommending its own lane as owner would be doing exactly that. Ownership is F13's. This seat records conditions, not a claim on the seat.
the_ownership_question.one_clock_rule: wherever ownership lands, exactly one component may compute a day-count. Everything else reads it.
